# README.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/README.md

# Codex Discord Rich Presence

A local Rust runtime that publishes Codex activity to Discord and shows the same state in a terminal dashboard. One binary for Windows, macOS and Linux, with no analytics telemetry.

<div align="center">
<img src="assets/branding/codex-readme-hero.png" alt="Codex Discord Rich Presence" width="100%">

[![Release v1.15.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Release-v1.15.0-171717)](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/releases/latest)
[![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-171717)](LICENSE)

[Install](#installation) · [Features](#features) · [Controls](#terminal-controls) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Documentation](docs/index.md)
</div>

## Overview

The runtime reads local Codex JSONL sessions and metadata. It can also read supported GPT sessions from OpenCode's local store. Session metadata has priority over launcher hints when identifying Codex App, ChatGPT App, CLI or VS Code activity.

The Discord identity remains Codex-owned. For a desktop analytics UI, arbitrary OpenCode providers and OpenCode Go account limits, use [Pulse](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Pulse-Analytics).

Release 1.15.0 keeps CDRP's files in its own folder instead of `~/.codex`, starts no background processes, adds GPT-6.1 Terra and a clickable footer link, and moves release tooling to `cargo xtask`. Its shared `codex-presence-core` is 2.0.1, and configuration schema 13 remains compatible. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for release details and rollback notes.

## Preview

![Codex presence, privacy, cache, context and terminal dashboard features](assets/branding/codex-feature-strip.png)

The foreground dashboard adapts to the terminal width. It uses a text wordmark, so no terminal image protocol is required. The [terminal UI guide](docs/ui/UI_SITEMAP.md) describes full, compact and minimal layouts.

## Features

| Data | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Model and effort | Preserve the recorded model and supported observed effort |
| Speed | Explicit session speed wins over local fallback settings |
| Context | Use observed context before local model cache or catalog defaults |
| Cost | Keep exact, partial and unavailable states separate |
| Quotas | Preserve actual provider windows, scope and reset timestamps |
| Credits | Show only reported balances or explicit unlimited status |
| Privacy | Publish only the fields enabled in the local configuration |

A formatted `$0.00` is a rounded known amount, not a substitute for missing cost. Unpublished pricing and incomplete telemetry remain unavailable or partial.

### Terminal controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `P` | Choose automatic detection or a manual plan label |
| `D` | Switch the desktop identity between Codex App and ChatGPT App |
| `V` | Edit the visibility of presence fields |
| `M` | Pause or resume Discord publication |
| `Q` / `Ctrl+C` | Exit the foreground runtime |

Plan and presence settings persist in `~/.codex-discord-presence/config.json` (`CODEX_PRESENCE_HOME` moves the folder). Everything the program writes stays in that folder; the Codex home is only read, and no background process is started. Pausing publication does not stop local monitoring.

### Configuration

The runtime keeps configuration under `CODEX_HOME`, or `~/.codex` by default.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CODEX_HOME` | Select a Codex home directory |
| `CODEX_PRESENCE_POLL_SECONDS` | Set the polling interval |
| `CODEX_PRESENCE_STALE_SECONDS` | Set the stale-session cutoff |
| `CODEX_PRESENCE_ACTIVE_STICKY_SECONDS` | Set the active-session retention window |
| `CODEX_PRESENCE_SURFACE` | Set a fallback surface: `cli`, `vscode` or `desktop` |
| `CODEX_PRESENCE_INCLUDE_WSL=1` | Opt in to WSL transcript discovery on Windows |
| `CODEX_PRESENCE_EFFICIENCY_MODE=0` | Opt out of Windows Efficiency mode before launch |

WSL scanning stays off unless requested. Surface overrides do not replace authoritative session metadata. See the [local schema](docs/database/schema.md) for configuration and snapshot fields.

On supported Windows versions, the runtime requests EcoQoS and Idle process priority for itself. It does not change the machine's power plan or another application's priority. Windows controls whether Task Manager displays a leaf indicator; other systems continue without this policy. See [Windows Efficiency mode](docs/windows-efficiency.md) for the read-only verifier and API contract.

## Supported surfaces

| Surface | Presence identity |
| --- | --- |
| Codex CLI | `Codex CLI` |
| Codex VS Code extension | `Codex VS Code Extension` |
| Codex desktop sessions | Selected `Codex App` or `ChatGPT App` design |
| Supported OpenCode-hosted GPT sessions | Codex-owned desktop identity |

Only Codex/OpenAI identities and assets publish. OpenCode support does not make this a general-purpose provider dashboard.

## Requirements

- The desktop Discord client, running and signed in, for Rich Presence publication.
- Local Codex sessions, or supported GPT sessions in OpenCode's local store.
- A terminal for the live dashboard.
- A matching release binary: Windows x64/ARM64, Linux x64, or macOS Intel/Apple Silicon.
- Rust 1.99.1 and a native linker only when building from source. Development checks also use cargo-nextest and cargo-audit.

Windows, macOS and Linux binaries are published. A native build or release smoke check does not imply every desktop environment has been manually tested.

## Installation

Download the matching binary from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/releases/latest). Verify it against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Windows releases also include architecture-specific SPDX software bills of materials.

### Windows

For x64, run in PowerShell:

```powershell
.\codex-discord-rich-presence-windows-x64.exe doctor
.\codex-discord-rich-presence-windows-x64.exe status
.\codex-discord-rich-presence-windows-x64.exe
```

Use `codex-discord-rich-presence-windows-arm64.exe` on ARM64. If a launcher hides the console, open Windows Terminal explicitly:

```powershell
wt -w new new-tab .\codex-discord-rich-presence-windows-x64.exe
```

### macOS

Choose `codex-discord-rich-presence-macos-arm64` for Apple Silicon or `codex-discord-rich-presence-macos-x64` for Intel. For Apple Silicon:

```sh
chmod +x codex-discord-rich-presence-macos-arm64
./codex-discord-rich-presence-macos-arm64 doctor
./codex-discord-rich-presence-macos-arm64
```

### Linux, including Arch and CachyOS

Use `codex-discord-rich-presence-linux-x64` on x86-64:

```sh
chmod +x codex-discord-rich-presence-linux-x64
./codex-discord-rich-presence-linux-x64 doctor
./codex-discord-rich-presence-linux-x64
```

Arch and CachyOS use the same binary; no AUR package is claimed. To build natively on Arch-based systems, install `base-devel`, Rust 1.99.1, `clang` and `mold`, then run `cargo build --release` from this repository. Source builds also support other targets with the matching Rust target and toolchain.

Keep Discord open for publication. The last command in each example opens the foreground dashboard; `status` and `doctor` are one-shot diagnostics.

### Commands

Use the downloaded filename in place of `codex-discord-rich-presence` below, or put it on your PATH under that name.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `codex-discord-rich-presence` | Open the foreground dashboard |
| `codex-discord-rich-presence status` | Print one operational snapshot |
| `codex-discord-rich-presence doctor` | Check setup and runtime requirements |
| `codex-discord-rich-presence codex` | Run Codex as a child and follow its lifecycle |
| `codex-discord-rich-presence discord-proof` | Send and clear an activity, then print a sanitized Discord acknowledgement proof |

## Updating

Exit the runtime, verify the new release's checksum, replace the binary and run `doctor` before restarting. Read the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for configuration and core compatibility. Keep the previous executable if you need to roll back; do not assume an older binary understands a newer configuration schema.

## Removal

Exit the runtime to clear its activity, then remove the downloaded binary and any launcher you created. Configuration and metrics remain under `CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex`; remove only the presence files you no longer need. Do not delete the Codex home directory, sessions or credentials to uninstall this runtime. See the [schema map](docs/database/schema.md) for owned file names.

## Project structure

```text
src/                         Runtime, CLI, Discord IPC, TUI and model catalog
crates/codex-presence-core/   UI-free usage and Discord composition contracts
xtask/                       Local checks and release tooling
assets/branding/             Codex/OpenAI visual assets
scripts/                     Platform-specific support tools
tests/integration/           Cross-module regressions
docs/                        Runtime, schema, UI and release guides
releases/                    Ignored local release outputs
```

## Development

Checks run locally; the GitHub release workflow is manual-only. Start with `cargo xtask check` before proposing a change.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Full local gate | `cargo xtask check` |
| Format / check format | `cargo fmt --all` / `cargo fmt --all -- --check` |
| Lint | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` |
| Rust tests | `cargo nextest run --workspace` |
| Release-tool tests | `cargo nextest run -p xtask` |
| Release compile | `cargo build --release` |
| Build release artifacts | `cargo xtask build-release` or `cargo xtask build-release --target <triple>` |
| Assemble release assets | `cargo xtask release-assets` |
| Generate / check language-model docs | `cargo xtask llms` / `cargo xtask llms --check` |
| Validate changelog | `cargo xtask changelog check` |
| Extract changelog section | `cargo xtask changelog notes <version>` |
| Generate release body | `cargo xtask release-notes <version>` |
| Check / apply repository metadata | `cargo xtask meta --check` / `cargo xtask meta --apply` |
| Diagnostics from source | `cargo run -- status` / `cargo run -- doctor` |

The project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html), [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/2.0.0/) and [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/); see the [documentation index](docs/index.md), [test map](tests/index.md), [language-model map](llms.txt) and [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Read the [release procedure](docs/releasing.md) before creating a tag. Releases use annotated tags, an approved exact `main` commit and verified checksums. Published tags and assets are not replaced. A Windows cross-build alone does not prove native ARM64 execution.

## FAQ

### Does this upload my conversations?

No. It does not upload transcripts or send analytics telemetry. It publishes only the Discord fields you enable and performs the network requests required by its configured integration. Keep credentials and private prompts out of public issues. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) and report vulnerabilities through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/security/advisories/new).

### Why is cost missing or partial?

Unknown pricing and incomplete request telemetry are unavailable, not zero. A known subtotal can be partial; snapshots retain coverage and provenance. See the [runtime contract](docs/api/codex-presence.md).

### Can I pause Discord without stopping monitoring?

Yes. Press `M` in the terminal. The switch persists, clears Discord activity and leaves local monitoring running. Press `M` again to publish the current state.

### Does this replace Pulse?

No. This is the terminal runtime for Codex-owned presence. [Pulse](https://github.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Pulse-Analytics) provides a desktop analytics UI and broader provider support.

# docs/api/codex-presence.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/docs/api/codex-presence.md

# Codex Presence Runtime API

This document owns the local runtime contract exported by the daemon modules.

## Public Runtime Surfaces

| Module | Contract |
|:---|:---|
| `src/model.rs` | Resolves the bundled model catalog, aliases, display labels, effort/speed capabilities, context provenance, and verified rates |
| `src/session.rs` | Produces `CodexSessionSnapshot` from Codex JSONL and local OpenCode data |
| `src/cost.rs` | Applies local overrides and computes exact, partial, or unavailable token costs |
| `src/metrics.rs` | Aggregates session snapshots into a unified cost/cache/context report |
| `src/config.rs` | Owns schema-13 persistence, last-good runtime reload, the master presence switch, ordered composer, design, privacy, plan, and pricing overrides |
| `crates/codex-presence-core` | Owns semantic quota/credit telemetry plus deterministic two-line Discord composition without UI dependencies |
| `src/discord.rs` | Converts runtime state into Discord IPC activities and Codex asset identities, including idempotent pause/resume transitions |
| `src/ui.rs` | Renders the Ratatui terminal view from `RenderData` |

`src/model_catalog.json` is the single machine-readable owner for bundled model facts. It includes source URLs and a verification date. Consumers must use the exported model API instead of rebuilding model names, capabilities, or rates.

`discord::active_presence_presentation` and `idle_presence_presentation` own the public activity title, details, state, large asset, and optional small system signal. Discord IPC, previews, and vendored consumers must use this contract instead of rebuilding presentation strings.

## Opt-in live Discord proof

`discord-proof` is a diagnostic-only backend command. With Discord desktop
already running, it publishes one activity through the same surface selection,
asset resolution, and `DiscordIpcClient` path as the daemon, waits for the
`SET_ACTIVITY` acknowledgement, clears the activity, waits for the clear
acknowledgement, then emits a sanitized JSON artifact:

```text
codex-discord-presence discord-proof --output proof.json
```

The artifact records the exact outbound `SET_ACTIVITY` DTO, both accepted
replies, the selected public surface, and cost assertions. Known exact and partial
subtotals render as currency only when the cost field is public. Unavailable
values remain absent. The proof rejects missing enabled costs and unavailable
amounts. Coverage remains in the structured snapshot, not in the Discord label.
The command does not acquire the daemon single-instance lock and does not stop
Discord, Pulse, or any existing presence process.

## Adaptive Usage Contract

`codex-presence-core::usage` is the single owner for provider-neutral usage
data. `UsageLane` is one of `codex_subscription`, `open_ai_api`,
`claude_subscription`, `anthropic_api`, or `unknown`. A lane is selected only
from explicit `UsageSignal` evidence: a session JSONL marker by itself stays
`unknown`, and evidence from more than one provider lane is ambiguous and
stays fail-closed.

`UsageSource` carries the selected lane, a stable non-secret `stream_id`, and
the sorted/deduplicated signals. `UsageStream` keeps that source with its
envelopes, while `UsageSnapshotCollection` keeps each stream's snapshot
separate. Selection matches the requested `lane + stream_id` exactly; it never
falls back to another provider, account, or stream. The upstream runtime
continues to collect only local Codex session JSONL; no Claude or Anthropic
collector is enabled by this contract.

`RateLimits.windows` is an ordered dynamic list. The legacy primary/secondary
wire shape is accepted on read and normalized to this list, but new JSON emits
only `windows`. Labels are derived from each window's duration, so a missing
window is never fabricated. Within one stream, `GlobalAccount` credits take
precedence over individual/model credits. Equal-rank conflicting envelopes,
unknown lanes, and ambiguous sources return no effective selection.

The authenticated Codex app-server `account/rateLimits/read` response is parsed
by `parse_account_rate_limits_response` in the same core crate. The
`rateLimits` snapshot (including `rateLimitsByLimitId`) becomes `envelopes`,
while `result.rateLimitResetCredits` remains a separate
`RateLimitResetCreditsSummary`. Its `available_count` is authoritative; the
optional `credits` list preserves the protocol distinction between `null`
(only the count is known) and an empty list (details were fetched and none are
available). A Discord consumer may show only the count when it is positive and
must omit the field for a missing or zero summary; it must not infer access from
expiry, title, description, or reset type.

The wire contract is tracked against the official
[`RateLimitResetCreditsSummary`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/RateLimitResetCreditsSummary.ts),
[`RateLimitResetCredit`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/RateLimitResetCredit.ts),
[`RateLimitResetType`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/RateLimitResetType.ts),
and
[`RateLimitResetCreditStatus`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/RateLimitResetCreditStatus.ts)
definitions (verified 2026-08-02).

## GPT-5.6 Contract

| ID | Codex App label | Effective context | Ultra | Fast |
|:---|:---|---:|:---:|:---:|
| `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-blue`, `gpt-5.6-cyber-blue` | `5.6-Cyber-Blue` | Runtime-observed (`258_400` currently observed) | Yes | No |
| `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `gpt-daybreak-red`, `gpt-daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-5.6-cyber-red` | `5.6-Cyber-Red` | `400_000` | Yes | No |
| `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-sol` | `5.6 Sol` | `353_400` | Yes | Yes |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` | `5.6 Terra` | `353_400` | Yes | Yes |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | `5.6 Luna` | `353_400` | No | Yes |

The raw context is `372_000`; Codex App exposes 95% as usable context. Context resolution order is observed JSONL `model_context_window`, valid local `~/.codex/models_cache.json`, then the bundled catalog. Snapshots preserve `raw_window_tokens`, usable `window_tokens`, `effective_percent`, the selected `source`, and `raw_source` separately. The local cache reader is size- and count-bounded and falls back closed on malformed or implausible data.

Daybreak Blue has no bundled context, pricing, credit rates, or Fast capability: observed runtime context wins, and missing economics stay unavailable. Cyber Red uses the published `gpt-5.6-cyber` contract: 400K context, 128K max output, and a 272K long-context threshold. Cumulative session telemetry cannot prove which individual request crossed that threshold, so totals above it remain partial lower bounds rather than receiving an invented surcharge.

No public max-output, API context, cache-write credit rate, or Fast usage multiplier was verified for Sol, Terra, or Luna, so those fields remain absent rather than inheriting older GPT-5 constants. The OpenAI pricing page lists a long-context tier for all three (2x input and cache, 1.5x output above 272K input tokens in one request, checked 2026-11-07), so the catalog carries that threshold and the multipliers.

GPT-5.6 Sol is on a promotional price until 2026-11-30. The catalog keeps the promotional rates and does not guess the price after that date; re-verify the pricing page then. The Codex credit rates of the three models come from the 2026-07-09 rate card and were not re-verified on 2026-11-07.

## GPT-6 family contract

Verified 2026-10-16 against the official model pages for GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, and 2026-11-07 for GPT-6.1 Terra. The bundled `context.raw_tokens` is the Codex-usable fallback; `api_tokens`, `max_input_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` record API capability and never stand in for Codex capacity.

| ID | Label | Bundled Codex fallback (raw / usable) | API context / max input / max output | Codex efforts | Fast |
|:---|:---|---:|:---|:---|:---:|
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | `GPT-6.1 Sol` | `500_000` / `475_000` | `1_050_000` / `922_000` / `128_000` | `low`…`max`, `ultra` | Yes |
| `gpt-6.1-terra` | `GPT-6.1 Terra` | `500_000` / `475_000` | `1_050_000` / `922_000` / `128_000` | `low`…`max`, `ultra` | Yes |
| `gpt-6-sol` | `GPT-6 Sol` | `872_000` / `872_000` | `1_050_000` / `922_000` / `128_000` | `low`…`max`, `ultra` | Yes |
| `gpt-6-luna` | `GPT-6 Luna` | `872_000` / `872_000` | `1_050_000` / `922_000` / `128_000` | `low`…`max` | Yes |

- Context provenance stays observed JSONL, then local `models_cache.json`, then this fallback. The local inventory written 2026-10-03 lists `gpt-6.1-sol` at `272_000` raw with 95% usable, and that value wins over the fallback while it is present.
- The `gpt-6.1-sol` fallback of `500_000` follows secondary reports (orcarouter.ai, 2026-10-12, citing OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux) that Codex raised the default from 272K to 500K on 2026-10-12. No OpenAI primary page confirms it. The 95% usable share is carried over from the 272K inventory row.
- `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` use the local inventory value, 872K at 100%. `gpt-6-astra` still bundles the API-sized 1,050,000 fallback, while the same inventory reports 872K. That documented gap is unchanged.
- API reasoning efforts are separate from Codex efforts. The API pages list `low`, `medium` (default), `high`, `xhigh` and `max` for 6.1 Sol, and add `none` for 6 Sol and 6 Luna. Codex `ultra` is not an API effort.
- The API pages price Fast at 2x Standard. The Codex inventory describes Fast as "1.5x speed", which is a speed claim, not a price. 6.1 Sol Ultrafast (`service_tier: "ultrafast"`, 6x Standard) has no runtime speed mode, so the runtime does not price it as Ultrafast.
- No official Codex credit rate is recorded for the GPT-6 family, so `credit_rates` stays `null`.
- `gpt-6.1-terra` was released on 2026-10-26. Its bundled fallback is the Codex catalog value `context_window` `500_000` at the default 95% usable share (`475_000`); the same catalog entry allows up to `872_000` through `max_context_window`, which the runtime does not use. The efforts `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` and `ultra` and the `fast` speed tier come from that Codex entry (openai/codex commit `126a0ee92e`, `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`). Its Fast price is 2x Standard.

## Presentation

`ReasoningEffort` is owned by `model` and accepts `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, and `ultra`. The `low` display label is `Light`. Unsupported model/effort combinations are omitted from display.

Fast is session-scoped and stored independently from the canonical model id. JSONL `thread_settings_applied.thread_settings.service_tier=priority` sets `SessionSpeed::Fast` only when that model declares Fast support. Later turn-context records without a speed signal do not overwrite it. Presentation examples:

- `GPT-5.6 Sol · Max`
- `GPT-5.6 Sol · Max · ⚡ Fast`
- `GPT-5.6 Terra · Light`
- `GPT-5.6-Cyber-Blue · High`
- `GPT-5.6-Cyber-Red · Ultra`

`gpt-5.6` is an alias of Sol. No `gpt-5.6-pro` model is invented; Pro remains a plan/reasoning concept outside the model family.

## Surface Identity

Session metadata is authoritative. `Codex Desktop`, `codex_work_desktop`, and OpenCode map to desktop, `codex_vscode` maps to `Codex VS Code Extension`, and `codex-tui` maps to `Codex CLI`. When metadata is absent, the runtime requires an extension-host process, an OpenCode marker, or the explicit `CODEX_PRESENCE_SURFACE=cli|vscode|desktop` override; generic VS Code terminal variables and unrelated open apps never change the identity.

Config schema 13 stores the shared `presence_enabled` master switch, `display.desktop_presence_design`, and the ordered ten-field composer:

| Value | Desktop label | Discord client id |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `codex_app` | `Codex App` | `1478395304624652345` |
| `chat_gpt_app` | `ChatGPT App` | `1470480085453770854` |

CLI and VS Code always use the shared `1470480085453770854` identity. Pressing `D` in Ratatui toggles and saves the desktop value; Discord reconnects when the selected client id changes.

Foreground TUI, headless, and Codex-wrapper loops reload `~/.codex-discord-presence/config.json` before every poll. Valid external edits replace the complete runtime config together. Invalid, missing, or transiently replaced files are logged and ignored so the process keeps its last valid configuration.

`presence_enabled` defaults to `true` during schema-11 migration. Pressing `M` in Ratatui or changing the same field in Pulse clears Discord activity once and reports `Paused`; session parsing, metrics, and the terminal dashboard continue locally. Re-enabling forces a fresh publish from the current session.

## Privacy Fields

Press `V` in Ratatui to edit the ten persisted Discord fields: project name, Git branch, model, activity, token count, cost, semantic quotas, Credits, context usage, and systems. `Shift+↑/↓` reorders the selected field. Context is independent from token count. Systems controls the small activity asset and its tooltip. Every edit is saved atomically and triggers a fresh public presentation before Discord publication.

Quota labels come only from each dynamic window's `window_minutes` value; an absent or malformed duration is omitted and no positional window is fabricated. Credits preserve the received decimal text; explicit zero and unlimited are displayable, while an absent or malformed object remains unavailable.

## Pricing

Standard API rates per one million tokens, checked against the OpenAI pricing page on 2026-11-07. Cache write is the 30-minute rate; `n/a` means the model has no separate cache-write price.

| Model | Input | Cache write | Cache read | Output | Long input / cache read / output |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---|
| `gpt-6-astra` | `$10.00` | `$12.50` | `$1.00` | `$50.00` | `$20.00` / `$2.00` / `$75.00` |
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | `$2.00` | `$2.50` | `$0.10` | `$10.00` | `$4.00` / `$0.20` / `$15.00` |
| `gpt-6.1-terra` | `$1.00` | `$1.25` | `$0.05` | `$5.00` | `$2.00` / `$0.10` / `$7.50` |
| `gpt-6-luna` | `$0.10` | `$0.125` | `$0.01` | `$0.50` | `$0.20` / `$0.02` / `$0.75` |
| `gpt-6-sol` | `$2.00` | `$2.50` | `$0.20` | `$10.00` | `$4.00` / `$0.40` / `$15.00` |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` (promotional until 2026-11-30) | `$4.00` | `$5.00` | `$0.40` | `$20.00` | `$8.00` / `$0.80` / `$30.00` |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` | `$2.00` | `$2.50` | `$0.20` | `$12.00` | `$4.00` / `$0.40` / `$18.00` |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | `$0.20` | `$0.25` | `$0.02` | `$1.20` | `$0.40` / `$0.04` / `$1.80` |
| `gpt-5.6-cyber` (Cyber Red) | `$12.50` | `$15.625` | `$1.25` | `$75.00` | none |
| `gpt-5.5` | `$5.00` | n/a | `$0.50` | `$30.00` | `$10.00` / `$1.00` / `$45.00` |
| `gpt-5.4` | `$2.50` | n/a | `$0.25` | `$15.00` | `$5.00` / `$0.50` / `$22.50` |
| `gpt-5.4-mini` | `$0.75` | n/a | `$0.075` | `$4.50` | none |
| `gpt-5.3-codex` | `$1.75` | n/a | `$0.175` | `$14.00` | none |
| `gpt-5.2` | `$1.75` | n/a | `$0.175` | `$14.00` | none |
| `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5` | `$1.25` | n/a | `$0.125` | `$10.00` | none |
| `gpt-5-mini` | `$0.25` | n/a | `$0.025` | `$2.00` | none |
| `gpt-5-nano` | `$0.05` | n/a | `$0.005` | `$0.40` | none |

A request with more than 272K observed input tokens is billed at the long-context rates for the full request: 2x input and cache and 1.5x output. GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 publish long-context API rates too, but their Codex context window is 272K, the threshold itself, so no Codex request reaches them and the catalog does not apply them. `gpt-5.5-pro` and `codex-mini-latest` are also bundled but were not part of the 2026-11-07 check. Fast is 2x Standard for the GPT-6 family; GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 keep their catalog multipliers, and GPT-5.6 has no verified Fast multiplier, so a Fast GPT-5.6 cost stays partial.

Cyber Blue is intentionally absent from this table because no public pricing contract was verified.

`compute_cost_for_request()` takes `TokenUsage` and optional observed request input. It subtracts known cache reads and writes once from ordinary input and returns `PricingStatus`:

| Status | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `exact` | Every published price component has observed token telemetry |
| `partial` | The known subtotal excludes a published component absent from telemetry, currently GPT-5.6 cache writes in Codex JSONL |
| `unavailable` | No verified pricing or valid user override exists |

Unknown models never inherit a fallback rate. Discord emits known subtotals without coverage text and hides unavailable costs. Structured output retains the classification. OpenCode can produce an exact GPT-5.6 total because its database reports cache-write tokens separately.

The session tracker accumulates usage deltas with each observed model and speed. It uses aligned last-request input to resolve the context tier. Cumulative input never acts as a request size. Missing request boundaries keep the known subtotal partial. Requests with observed input over 272K use the documented long-context multipliers for Astra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4. GPT-5.3 Codex Spark remains unavailable instead of inheriting GPT-5.3 Codex rates because its current Codex credit rates are explicitly non-final.

## Prompt Cache Policy

The bundled policy records a 1,024-token eligibility minimum and a 30-minute minimum lifetime. It is metadata for analysis; the daemon does not infer unobserved cache writes.

## Local Files

| File | Purpose |
|:---|:---|
| `~/.codex/models_cache.json` | Current Codex App model context metadata |
| `~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl` | Codex sessions, read only. A full walk runs every 30 seconds; polls in between read today's and yesterday's folders and the recent files |
| `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode*.db` | OpenCode-hosted Codex sessions, opened read-only and as immutable when OpenCode is closed, so no `-wal` or `-shm` file appears |
| `~/.codex-discord-presence/config.json` | Runtime config and pricing overrides |
| `~/.codex-discord-presence/plan-cache.json` | Last detected plan, written only when it changes |
| `~/.codex-discord-presence/instance.lock`, `instance.json` | Single-instance lock and its owner |

`~/.codex` is only read. The Git branch comes from `.git/HEAD` and the dashboard redraws only when its content changes. Without a terminal (autostart, a launcher) the program runs with no window; set `CODEX_PRESENCE_OPEN_TERMINAL=1` to open one instead.

## Unreleased session-cost corrections

`src/session/costing.rs` owns event accumulation, repeated-event rejection, cache-write totals and multimodel subtotals. `cache_write_input_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens` remain optional. Missing model tariffs do not erase previously known cost.

The shared compositor reserves space for enabled cost fields when a preceding model label fills the Discord line. The field-order and privacy contracts stay unchanged. The [Astra model card](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra) and [per-run cost arithmetic](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/articles/per_run_spending_controller_responses_api) were checked on 2026-09-20 for request-level context multipliers and disjoint token categories.

# docs/database/schema.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/docs/database/schema.md

# Local Schema Map

All data stays on the user's machine. The daemon reads Codex/OpenCode local state and writes only config plus local report artifacts.

## Config

Path: `~/.codex-discord-presence/config.json` (or `$CODEX_PRESENCE_HOME/config.json`). The first start moves the file from `~/.codex`, where releases up to 1.11 kept it.

Current schema version: `13`.

| Owner | Fields |
|:---|:---|
| Identity | Shared CLI/VS Code client id, Codex App desktop client id, and asset keys |
| Runtime | `presence_enabled`, poll interval, stale cutoff, active sticky window |
| Display | `desktop_presence_design` (`codex_app` or `chat_gpt_app`), terminal logo mode/path, large/small image text, and the ordered `presence_layout` with field zone and label style |
| Pricing | Model aliases and overrides |
| Plan | Local plan override and preset selection. Manual tiers include `Pro 5x ($100/month)` and `Pro 20x ($200/month)`; legacy `pro` maps to Pro 20x. |
| Privacy | Project, branch, model, activity, tokens, cost, semantic quotas, Credits, context, systems, activity target, and global private-mode flags. |

Schemas 11 and 12 migrate atomically to schema 13. Existing visibility choices are preserved, Credits defaults on, and the ten fields receive a validated deterministic order. Pulse and every standalone runtime mode write and reload this same atomic file; no secondary control file or process-takeover state exists. Failed reloads preserve the last valid in-memory value.

## Session Snapshot

`CodexSessionSnapshot` is the canonical active-session shape.

| Group | Fields |
|:---|:---|
| Identity | `session_id`, `cwd`, `project_name`, `git_branch`, `originator`, `source` |
| Model | `model`, `reasoning_effort`, session-scoped `speed`, and `context_window` with source |
| Usage | token totals including optional `cache_write_tokens_total`, backward-compatible `total_cost_usd`, optional `known_cost_usd`, `pricing_source`, `pricing_status`, `cost_attribution`, reconciliation flag, and `cost_breakdown` |
| Activity | `activity`, `last_activity`, token-event timestamps |
| Limits | `limits`, all global/model-scoped `rate_limit_envelopes`, semantic `window_minutes`, and optional account `credits` |
| Source | `source_file` |

## Cost Breakdown

| Field | Type | Notes |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `input_cost_usd` | number | Non-cached input cost |
| `cache_write_cost_usd` | number | Known cache-write cost; zero is not presented as exact when write telemetry is absent |
| `cached_input_cost_usd` | number | Cached-input read cost |
| `output_cost_usd` | number | Output cost |
| `cached_input_savings_usd` | number | Cached discount versus full input price |

## Metrics Snapshot

The dashboard keeps this snapshot in memory; it is not written to disk.

| Field | Notes |
|:---|:---|
| `totals.input_tokens` | Total input including cached tokens |
| `totals.cached_input_tokens` | Prompt-cache read tokens |
| `totals.output_tokens` | Output tokens |
| `totals.known_cost_usd` | Known subtotal, absent when no verified component can be priced |
| `totals.pricing_status` | Aggregate `exact`, `partial`, or `unavailable` state |
| `totals.complete_sessions` | Sessions with complete verified pricing |
| `totals.incomplete_sessions` | Sessions with missing pricing components or unavailable pricing |
| `totals.unavailable_sessions` | Subset with no known subtotal |
| `totals.pricing_sources` | Counts for catalog, alias, user override, provider report, unavailable, and legacy provenance |
| `totals.cache_hit_ratio` | `cached_input_tokens / input_tokens` |
| `cost_breakdown.cached_input_savings_usd` | Aggregate cached-input savings |
| `by_model[].cache_hit_ratio` | Per-model cache health |

## Context Windows

`ContextWindowSnapshot` stores usable window, used/remaining tokens, remaining percentage, and source. GPT-5.6 has 372,000 raw inventory tokens and 353,400 usable tokens at 95% in Codex 0.144.0. Resolution order is observed JSONL, valid local `models_cache.json`, then the bundled catalog. The runtime does not invent GPT-5.6 API context, long-context thresholds, or max output values when those facts are not published.

# docs/ui/UI_SITEMAP.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/docs/ui/UI_SITEMAP.md

# Terminal UI Sitemap

The foreground terminal is a Ratatui dashboard over the same daemon runtime that publishes Discord Rich Presence.

## Layout Modes

| Mode | Trigger | Shape |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Full | `>=118x32` | Header, active session, quota/context, usage snapshot, spend sparkline, recent sessions |
| Compact | `>=72x18` | Header, active session, quota/context, recent sessions |
| Minimal | Smaller terminals | Header, active session, short recent list |

## Widgets

| Widget | Contract |
|:---|:---|
| Runtime header | Large centered Codex wordmark, local-first subtitle, animated spinner, mode, Discord status, poll cadence, selected desktop design |
| Active session | Project, branch, model, reasoning effort, Fast state, cost, token triplet, usable/raw context, activity target |
| Quota + context | Primary/secondary gauges, plan label, Fast label, source freshness, OAuth/API context copy |
| Usage snapshot | Total cost, cache hit ratio, cached-input savings, uptime, spend sparkline by model |
| Recent sessions | Responsive list of recent project/model/token summaries |
| Plan picker | Centered selector with Auto Detect plus Free, Go, Plus, Pro 5x, Pro 20x, Business, and Enterprise presets |
| Master presence | `M` immediately persists pause/resume; paused mode clears Discord once while local monitoring stays active |
| Desktop design | `D` immediately toggles and persists `Codex App` / `ChatGPT App`; the next publish reconnects to the matching Discord application |
| Footer | Author credit plus `M`, `V`, `P`, `D`, and quit actions with the current presence state; collapses safely on narrow terminals |

## Theme

The theme is Codex dark with a restrained black-and-white terminal palette:

| Role | Use |
|:---|:---|
| White | Codex identity, selected plan, active model, connected state, sparklines |
| Gray | Metadata, inactive states, medium quota, footer text |
| Dark gray | Panel borders and structural separation |

## Motion

Animation is tick-driven by `RenderData.banner_phase`. The frame signature includes `banner_phase`, presence enabled/paused state, desktop design, active model/effort/speed, limits, metrics, and picker state so the runtime redraws only when visible state changes.

## Logo Policy

`assets/branding/codex-app.png` and `assets/branding/chatgpt-app.jpg` are the canonical desktop preview sources. The terminal header intentionally uses a text wordmark instead of duplicating either app icon, so the UI stays readable and the selected design remains a semantic status label.

## Accessibility + Resilience

- No mouse dependency.
- Compact and minimal modes avoid horizontal overflow.
- Quota colors are paired with text labels and percentages.
- Idle copy reports the selected desktop design without collapsing CLI and VS Code into one label.
- Paused copy states that Discord publication is off while local monitoring remains active.
- If metrics are not ready, the widget renders a warm-up state instead of blank space.

# docs/windows-efficiency.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/docs/windows-efficiency.md

# Windows Efficiency mode

This reference describes the process policy used by the Windows builds. It is a scheduling request, not a measured promise about energy savings.

The application calls `SetProcessInformation` with `ProcessPowerThrottling`, sets the execution-speed control/state bits and selects `IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS`. It changes only its own process. Unrelated power-throttling flags remain intact. If the priority update fails, the previous throttling state is restored. Unsupported API calls do not prevent startup.

Windows 11 interprets the execution-speed request as EcoQoS. Task Manager owns the leaf indicator; application code does not fabricate it. Other operating systems keep their normal scheduling policy.

## Verify a running process

Use `cargo xtask windows-efficiency --pid 1234`, replacing the example ID with the application's PID. A successful enabled state reports `eco_qos: true`, `idle_priority: true` and priority class `64`. The verifier opens a query-only process handle and does not change the process.

## Opt out

Set `CODEX_PRESENCE_EFFICIENCY_MODE=0` before launching the application. `false`, `off` and `disabled` are also accepted. The normal default requests Efficiency mode. This does not modify the machine's power plan or other applications.

## Sources

- [Microsoft: Quality of Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/quality-of-service)
- [Microsoft: SetProcessInformation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-setprocessinformation)

The implementation uses the installed Windows SDK's 12-byte `PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_STATE` layout. Local tests verify the ABI constants and option parsing; process readback verifies the applied policy.

# PRIVACY.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/PRIVACY.md

# Privacy

`codex-discord-presence` runs locally and reads local Codex session files from `~/.codex/sessions`.

## Data Processed

- project path/name
- git branch (derived locally)
- model id/name
- token counters
- usage windows (5h / 7d)

## Data Flow

1. Data is parsed locally from local files.
2. Presence payload is sent to local Discord desktop via IPC.
3. No built-in analytics/telemetry endpoint is used by this project.

## Data Storage

- Config: `~/.codex/discord-presence-config.json`
- Lock file: `~/.codex/codex-discord-presence.lock`

No persistent cloud storage is performed by this application.

# CONTRIBUTING.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing

Thanks for contributing to Codex Discord Rich Presence (`codex-discord-presence`).

## Development workflow

1. Fork and create a feature branch from `main`.
2. Keep changes focused and production-oriented.
3. Add or update the cheapest test that proves each behavior change.
4. Run `cargo xtask check` locally before proposing the change.
5. Open a PR with the problem, implementation, test evidence and risk/backout notes.

Checks run locally. There is no per-push or per-PR CI; the GitHub release workflow is manual-only.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Full local gate | `cargo xtask check` |
| Format / check format | `cargo fmt --all` / `cargo fmt --all -- --check` |
| Lint | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` |
| Rust tests | `cargo nextest run --workspace` |
| Release-tool tests | `cargo nextest run -p xtask` |
| Release compile | `cargo build --release` |
| Release artifacts | `cargo xtask build-release [--target <triple>]` |
| Release asset assembly | `cargo xtask release-assets` |
| Generate / check documentation maps | `cargo xtask llms` / `cargo xtask llms --check` |
| Check changelog / extract section | `cargo xtask changelog check` / `cargo xtask changelog notes <version>` |
| Generate release body | `cargo xtask release-notes <version>` |
| Check / apply repository metadata | `cargo xtask meta --check` / `cargo xtask meta --apply` |
| Diagnostics | `cargo run -- status` / `cargo run -- doctor` |

See the [documentation index](docs/index.md) and [test map](tests/index.md) for contracts and focused checks.

## Commit conventions

Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) so intent is machine-readable and release notes remain reviewable:

| Prefix | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `feat:` | New user-visible behavior |
| `fix:` | Correctness defect |
| `perf:` | Measured performance improvement |
| `refactor:` | Internal change with no behavior change |
| `docs:` | Documentation only |
| `test:` | Test-only change |
| `chore:` | Tooling, dependency or release maintenance |

Add `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer only when a public CLI, configuration, core API or Discord output contract is intentionally incompatible. Keep the subject imperative and under 72 characters.

Versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Write user-visible changes under the six [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/2.0.0/) types: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed and Security.

## Code quality expectations

- Keep modules cohesive and dependency boundaries clear.
- Prefer explicit error handling with actionable messages.
- Keep behavior deterministic and cross-platform.
- Preserve single-binary UX.
- Keep `codex-presence-core` UI-free and deterministic. The binary and downstream Pulse integration must not create a second telemetry owner.
- Keep unknown prices, limits and context values unavailable, never zero.
- Do not commit credentials, private session evidence, local settings or agent instruction files.

## PR checklist

- [ ] No unrelated refactors bundled.
- [ ] Tests prove changed behavior at the public seam when modules interact.
- [ ] Docs and changelog updated for user-visible changes.
- [ ] Local gate passes, with platform coverage and limitations recorded.
- [ ] No secrets, private data or local agent state in committed files.

## Release contract

Tags and release assets are immutable. Before an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag is approved:

1. Synchronize the product and core version surfaces required by the release contract.
2. Add the matching changelog section with one summary paragraph and run `cargo xtask changelog check` and `cargo nextest run -p xtask`.
3. Prove configuration migrations, Windows runtime behavior and Linux/macOS builds on the appropriate platforms.
4. Generate and validate Windows SPDX software bills of materials and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
5. Record the exact approved commit SHA. Never mutate an existing tag or published release asset.

Release titles and prose may be corrected without changing tags or assets. The title is `Codex Discord Rich Presence vX.Y.Z`; the body is the matching changelog summary and sections verbatim, without another title, asset list, integrity section or compare link. Only sections longer than 150 lines may append the asset, integrity and full-changelog material.

Read the [release procedure](docs/releasing.md) before promotion. Local development must stop before tag, push, PR or release creation unless the maintainer explicitly approves promotion.

# tests/index.md

# Tests

`cargo xtask check` runs the full local gate. Run focused checks while working, then the full gate before proposing a change. Results below are **pending** until the lead records dated validation after merging the parallel lanes.

[Local gates](#local-gates) · [Runtime regressions](#runtime-regressions) · [Release and documentation](#release-and-documentation)

## Local gates

| What it proves | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Formatting matches rustfmt | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | pending |
| Workspace and targets pass warning-denying lint | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | pending |
| Runtime, shared core and tooling regressions pass | `cargo nextest run --workspace` | pending |
| Native optimized binary builds | `cargo build --release` | pending |
| Dependency audit has no unapproved findings | `cargo audit --deny warnings` | pending |

## Runtime regressions

| What it proves | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog identities, aliases, efforts, Standard/Fast pricing and context precedence | `cargo nextest run --test integration model_contract` | pending |
| Model labels preserve reasoning, speed and Codex-owned identities | `cargo nextest run --test integration model_display` | pending |
| Schema 13 migration, privacy defaults and external configuration reload | `cargo nextest run --test integration config_migration` | pending |
| Per-event costs preserve model, speed, cache writes, known subtotals and long-context request boundaries without double counting | `cargo nextest run --lib costing` | pending |
| Session parsing, incremental reads, activity, ranking and scanner resource bounds | `cargo nextest run --lib session` | pending |
| Shared provider lanes, quotas, reset credits and deterministic composition stay isolated | `cargo nextest run -p codex-presence-core` | pending |
| Public Discord fields respect privacy, identity, cost coverage and line limits | `cargo nextest run --lib discord` | pending |
| Terminal layouts, plan picker, design, privacy editor and pause/resume | `cargo nextest run --lib ui` | pending |
| Child ownership, takeover and process identity checks | `cargo nextest run --lib process_guard` | pending |
| Background probes use timeouts and silent Windows launchers | `cargo nextest run --lib util` | pending |
| OpenCode sessions keep their own usage provenance | `cargo nextest run --lib opencode` | pending |
| Windows WSL scanning stays opt-in | `cargo nextest run --lib windows_wsl` | pending |
| Process-local Windows Efficiency mode option and ABI contracts | `cargo nextest run --lib power` | pending |

The integration seams live in [integration/](integration/). Module-local tests stay beside their implementation. Tests that cross module boundaries belong in integration regressions. A passing non-Windows build does not prove Windows runtime behavior.

## Release and documentation

| What it proves | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release metadata, approval, target, assets, architecture, checksums and workflow contracts | `cargo nextest run -p xtask` | pending |
| Changelog uses the six standard sections, summaries and ordered version links | `cargo xtask changelog check` | pending |
| Published body is the version's changelog section without wrapper headings | `cargo xtask release-notes 1.11.3` | pending |
| Generated language-model maps match their manifest and documents | `cargo xtask llms --check` | pending |
| GitHub description and topics match repository metadata | `cargo xtask meta --check` | pending |

The [release procedure](../docs/releasing.md) owns native smoke checks, PE-machine validation, SPDX software bills of materials, checksums and immutable publication. `discord-proof` is an explicit live operation: it sends an activity and clears it again. It is not part of an offline unit-test run.

# docs/releasing.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/docs/releasing.md

# Release procedure

Releases are immutable and bound to a protected `main` commit. Quality checks run locally, not in GitHub Actions: there is no per-push or per-PR CI, and the Release workflow is manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`), so pushing a tag does not trigger it. Run the local gate with `cargo xtask check` and build locally, or dispatch the workflow by hand. The operator approval step uses the local authenticated GitHub CLI, so an administration token is never stored in Actions. Local implementation does not imply promotion.

Every check and release step is a Rust command in the `xtask` crate. PowerShell is not needed on any platform.

## Commands

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Full local gate (format, clippy, nextest, changelog, llms, release contract of the checkout, RustSec audit) | `cargo xtask check` |
| Release-script tests | `cargo nextest run -p xtask` |
| Validate the changelog format | `cargo xtask changelog check` |
| Print one changelog section | `cargo xtask changelog notes <version>` |
| Regenerate or verify `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` | `cargo xtask llms` / `cargo xtask llms --check` |
| Compare or apply the GitHub description and topics | `cargo xtask meta --check` / `cargo xtask meta --apply` |
| Validate tag, Cargo version, README badge, contract and changelog | `cargo xtask release-contract --tag vX.Y.Z` |
| Print the release notes (body), or the title | `cargo xtask release-notes <version>` / `cargo xtask release-notes <version> --title` |
| Build, package, verify and checksum the host target | `cargo xtask build-release` |
| Same for chosen targets (one operating system per run) | `cargo xtask build-release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` |
| Run `--version` and `doctor` on a built executable | `cargo xtask smoke --artifact <path>` |
| Assemble the ten published assets from downloaded artifacts | `cargo xtask release-assets --artifact-root <dir> --output-directory <dir>` |
| Approve the exact commit SHA | `cargo xtask approve-release --sha <40-character-main-sha>` |
| Check the approved target, protected checks and latest ordering | `cargo xtask release-target --tag vX.Y.Z --version X.Y.Z --sha <sha> --approved-sha <sha> --is-prerelease false` |
| Check a Windows executable's PE machine | `cargo xtask check-pe --artifact <exe> --architecture x64` |
| Generate and verify a Windows SPDX SBOM | `cargo xtask sbom ...` / `cargo xtask check-sbom ...` |
| Read the efficiency policy of a running process (Windows) | `cargo xtask windows-efficiency --pid <pid>` |

`approve-release` and `release-target` read the repository slug from `.github/repository.toml`. Pass `--repository owner/name` to override it. Every command prints one JSON line (or a short text line) on success and exits with code 1 and a message on failure.

## Version surfaces

`scripts/release-contract.json` is the machine-readable owner for the candidate product version, core version, config schema, checksum manifest, and both Windows target, artifact, SBOM and PE-machine contracts. For v1.15.0:

- binary and workspace: 1.15.0;
- `codex-presence-core`: 2.0.1;
- config schema: 13.

The tag version, Cargo metadata, README release badge (`Release v<version>`), changelog section and release contract must agree before preflight succeeds.

## Release notes

The GitHub release has the title `CDRP <version>`, short enough for the Releases list, and a body that is the matching `CHANGELOG.md` section, unchanged: the summary paragraph and the Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed and Security sections. The body has no `#` or `##` heading, no asset list, no integrity section and no compare link, because GitHub shows the title, the assets and the checksums next to the notes.

Only a section longer than 150 lines also gets three closing sections: Release assets, Integrity and Full changelog.

Preview the notes before tagging:

```bash
cargo xtask release-notes 1.11.3
```

GitHub lets maintainers edit the title and notes of a published immutable release. Only the tag and the assets are locked. To correct a published release, run `gh release edit vX.Y.Z --title "CDRP X.Y.Z" --notes-file <file>`. See [Immutable releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/immutable-releases).

## Required proof

1. Run `cargo xtask check`. It runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features`, the changelog check and `llms --check`. The `xtask` tests cover the metadata, approval, target, asset, PE, SBOM, notes and workflow contracts.
2. Run the release build and `cargo audit --deny warnings`.
3. Prove schema 12 to 13 migration and parser fixtures independent of the user profile.
4. On Windows, exercise `status`, `doctor`, TUI persistence, Fast, semantic quota windows, Credits, and real Discord publication.
5. Keep Linux and macOS compile and test gates green.
6. Install Rust targets `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` plus the MSVC ARM64 toolset, then run `cargo xtask build-release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`. The output lands in `releases/windows/`, which must be empty before the run.
7. The build validates PE machines `0x8664` and `0xAA64`, generates architecture-specific SPDX SBOMs, and includes all nine payloads in `SHA256SUMS.txt` (ten published assets including the manifest).
8. Before closing Windows ARM64 support, run `cargo xtask smoke` on the native `windows-11-arm` release job. A local x64-hosted cross-build does not substitute for that proof.

## Publish

1. Confirm the intended `main` commit has all required platform checks green.
2. Approve that exact commit:

   ```bash
   cargo xtask approve-release --sha <40-character-main-sha>
   ```

3. Create and push an annotated tag pointing to the approved commit:

   ```bash
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z <40-character-main-sha> -m "vX.Y.Z"
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

4. Publish the release. The Release workflow is manual-only, so pushing the tag does not start it. Either build and publish locally (`cargo xtask build-release`, then `gh release create vX.Y.Z <assets> --title "$(cargo xtask release-notes X.Y.Z --title)" --notes-file <(cargo xtask release-notes X.Y.Z)`), or dispatch the workflow by hand from the Actions tab for the tagged commit. On dispatch it rechecks tag ancestry, the approved SHA, version ordering, artifacts, both Windows SPDX SBOMs and PE machines, and SHA-256 digests before publishing once.
5. Verify the public release and then clear the one-use approval:

   ```bash
   gh variable delete RELEASE_APPROVED_SHA --repo xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence
   ```

Never move a published tag or replace a published asset. Publish a new patch version when a correction to the code or the binaries is required. Corrections to the title or the notes are edits, as described above.

# CHANGELOG.md

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xt0n1-t3ch/Codex-Discord-Rich-Presence/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/2.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Version numbers describe compatibility of the CLI and its commands, the configuration schema, the Discord presence output and the `codex-presence-core` API. A major version signals incompatible public changes, a minor version adds compatible behavior, and a patch fixes compatible behavior. The shared core has its own version; each release records core and schema compatibility when established.

## [Unreleased]

## [1.15.0] - 2026-11-07

CDRP 1.15.0 keeps its files in its own folder instead of `~/.codex`, starts no background processes, adds GPT-6.1 Terra, and moves release tooling to Rust. The shared core stays at 2.0.1 and configuration schema 13 is unchanged.

### Added

- GPT-6.1 Terra model identity, context limits and Standard/Fast pricing.
- `cargo xtask` for local checks, documentation, changelog, metadata and release tasks.
- Generated llms.txt and llms-full.txt documentation maps and CITATION.cff.

### Changed

- Align GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna rates with the published pricing table.
- Apply long-context pricing to requests above 272,000 input tokens for GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4: 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output rates.
- Match Pulse release notes: one summary paragraph and categorized changes without duplicated titles, asset lists, integrity sections or compare links.
- Use Rust 1.99.1, rusqlite 0.41 and ureq 3, with faster development builds.
- Replace PowerShell release scripts and their tests with Rust tooling.
- Follow Keep a Changelog 2.0.0.
- Describe every `cargo xtask` command and argument in `--help`, and document every module and the public items of the shared core.
- Keep every file the program writes in `~/.codex-discord-presence` (`CODEX_PRESENCE_HOME`). The first start moves the config and plan cache out of `~/.codex` and removes the old lock and metrics files; the Codex home is only read.
- Read the Git branch from `.git/HEAD` instead of running `git` on every poll, list WSL distros once per process, and read the launching process chain from `/proc` on Linux instead of running `ps`.
- Walk every session folder at most every 30 seconds; polls in between read today's and yesterday's folders and the recent files.
- Redraw the dashboard only when its content changes, write the plan cache only when the plan changes, and re-send an unchanged Discord activity every 30 seconds instead of every 2.
- Run without a window when started without a terminal; `CODEX_PRESENCE_OPEN_TERMINAL=1` opens one.
- Replace the author line in the dashboard footer with a clickable "Endorse at" link to this repository (OSC 8), shortened or dropped when the terminal is narrow.

### Removed

- Unused `ContextSource::Event` and `ContextSource::Catalog` aliases and duplicated OpenAI plan label helpers. Configuration files that use `event` or `catalog` still load.
- The metrics JSON and Markdown files rewritten every 10 seconds; the dashboard keeps metrics in memory.

### Fixed

- End daemon child processes with their parent on Linux.
- Check the target operating system instead of the host in build scripts.
- Repair the corrupted build-command path in the README and document `cargo xtask build-release`.
- Stop leaving `-wal` and `-shm` files next to OpenCode's database.
- Keep tests out of the user's Codex home.
- Treat a release up to 1.11 that still holds its lock in the Codex home as the running instance, so an upgrade never runs two presences at once, and keep that lock until it is released.
- Isolate the presence folder (`CODEX_PRESENCE_HOME`) as well as the Codex home in `cargo xtask smoke`, so a smoke run never touches the real configuration.
- Build the macOS ARM64 release on `macos-15`; GitHub retired the `macos-14` runner.
- Run the release contract of the checkout and the RustSec audit in `cargo xtask check`, so a release no longer stops at preflight for something the local gate could see.

### Security

- Update rustls-webpki to 0.103.16 or later and webpki-roots to 1.0.10 or later for RUSTSEC-2026-0381 and RUSTSEC-2026-0382, also proposed in PR #56 by @nekotyy.

## [1.11.3] - 2026-10-17

GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna support with bounded scanner memory and child processes. Runtime 1.11.3 keeps `codex-presence-core` 2.0.1, its public API, configuration schema 13, Discord identity rules and privacy controls. Costs remain telemetry-based estimates, and the reported GPT-6.1 Sol 500K Codex default had no OpenAI primary source in this release. Restore the previous executable to roll back; configuration and session data are not migrated or rewritten.

### Added

- Add GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna to the model catalog with API rates, Fast pricing, the 272K long-context surcharge and API context limits verified on 2026-10-16. The bundled context fallback uses Codex capacity, not the API maximum. GPT-6.1 Sol uses the reported 500K Codex default, which has no OpenAI primary source. Credit rates stay unavailable.

### Changed

- Replace the unmaintained `fs2` crate with standard-library file locks.
- Update semver-compatible dependencies, including `thiserror` 2.0.21, and update the `upload-artifact`, `download-artifact` and `rust-toolchain` action pins. Dependabot now proposes minor Cargo updates; major updates stay ignored.

### Fixed

- The session scanner checks file modification times before it opens a file. Files older than the stale and sticky cutoffs are not read. The parse cache keeps only the files that can still be included, plus the four newest files for account limits. A file that becomes active again is parsed from the start.
- Parse `~/.codex/models_cache.json` once for each modification instead of on every snapshot rebuild.
- Discard session lines longer than 16 MiB instead of buffering them, and stop copying each line.
- Expire tool calls that never complete after two hours, and keep at most 256 open calls per session.
- Resolve Git branches only for included sessions. Each Git probe has a two-second timeout; on expiry the probe is killed and reaped.
- In wrapper mode, kill and reap the `codex` child on every exit path, including an early error and Ctrl+C. On Windows, a kill-on-close job object also ends its process tree.
- Single-instance takeover checks that the PID in the instance file still runs the recorded executable before it terminates that process. On Windows, process checks and termination use native APIs instead of `tasklist` and PowerShell.

## [1.11.2] - 2026-09-19

Per-event session costing and reliable currency display, including partial known subtotals. Runtime 1.11.2 and `codex-presence-core` 2.0.1 preserve the public core API, configuration schema 13, Discord identity rules and privacy controls. Costs remain estimates from observed telemetry and selected rates; snapshots retain coverage and provenance. Restore the previous executable to roll back; configuration and session data are not migrated or rewritten.

### Fixed

- Accumulate session cost per usage event with model, speed and cache-write telemetry. Reject repeated events and preserve known multimodel subtotals.
- Apply supported long-context prices to observed request input, not accumulated session input.
- Publish enabled known monetary amounts as currency only, including partial subtotals, while keeping unavailable amounts absent and preserving coverage in snapshots.
- Reserve space for enabled costs in the shared Discord compositor when model labels are long.

### Security

- Update `rustls` to 0.23.45 to address RUSTSEC-2026-0285, which affects TLS 1.3 handshake validation.

## [1.11.1] - 2026-09-05

GPT-6 Astra support and Windows Efficiency mode, with warning-denying Linux builds restored. The v1.11.0 candidate did not publish release assets; this release includes its Astra, plan-precedence, monetary-display and Windows efficiency changes.

### Added

- Publish GPT-6 Astra identity, observed effort, context limits and Standard/Fast pricing with honest incomplete-cost handling.
- Publish process-local Windows Efficiency mode with an environment opt-out and read-only policy verifier.

### Fixed

- Make Windows Efficiency mode initialization an explicit no-op on other operating systems, so warning-denying Linux builds pass without suppressing lints. Windows EcoQoS behavior is unchanged.

## [1.11.0] - 2026-09-05

Unshipped candidate for GPT-6 Astra, plan precedence, monetary display and Windows Efficiency mode. The shared core remains 2.0.0, and Codex identity policy and configuration schema 13 are unchanged. Its changes ship in 1.11.1 instead.

### Added

- GPT-6 Astra identity, observed reasoning effort, a 1,050,000-token total context window, 922,000-token input limit and 128,000-token output limit.
- Astra Standard/Fast pricing resolution with explicit incomplete coverage and no invented subscription-credit rates.
- Windows Efficiency mode through process-local EcoQoS and Idle priority, with an environment opt-out and read-only process verifier.

### Changed

- README and release documentation explain the standalone terminal interface, source boundaries, Windows process policy and immutable artifact checks.
- The shared core remains version 2.0.0. Codex identity policy and config schema 13 are unchanged.

### Fixed

- Manual plan overrides resolve before automatic cache updates. Protocol pro maps to Pro 20x and prolite to Pro 5x; Edu and explicit plan aliases are supported.
- Unknown plan labels are omitted from public Discord model text when no reliable identification exists.
- Monetary display rounds to two decimal places while retaining full calculation precision and cost-completeness rules.

## [1.10.3] - 2026-08-25

Desktop sessions identified by `codex_work_desktop` retain the selected Codex App or ChatGPT App identity, alongside compatible dependency updates.

### Changed

- Refreshed `thiserror`, `serde`, and `ctrlc` to their compatible patch
  releases.

### Fixed

- Sessions whose originator is `codex_work_desktop` now retain the selected
  Codex App or ChatGPT App desktop identity even when their source is VS Code.

Daybreak Blue and Cyber Red model support and Windows ARM64 packaging, with release-preflight and publication checks corrected. Model contracts, displays, formatting, lint, workspace tests, release builds, Windows PE files, SBOMs and checksums were covered by local validation. Native Windows x64 and ARM64 version and doctor smoke checks remain mandatory in the manual release workflow.

### Added

- Native Daybreak Blue and Cyber Red model identities, canonical aliases, six reasoning efforts, runtime-first Blue context, and published Red context/pricing without invented Fast or credit rates.
- Windows ARM64 packaging with `codex-discord-rich-presence-windows-arm64.exe`, an architecture-specific SPDX SBOM, PE `0xAA64` validation, and native `windows-11-arm` release smoke.

### Changed

- Release assembly now publishes exactly ten assets: Windows x64 and ARM64 executables/SBOMs, Linux and macOS binaries, two logos, and one checksum manifest.
- Locked dependencies now resolve `anyhow` 1.0.104, `chrono` 0.4.45, and `thiserror` 2.0.19; transitive `lru` is updated to 0.18.2 to clear RUSTSEC-2026-0253.

### Fixed

- Release preflight clears the expected native-command exit status left by negative contract probes, so a fully passing suite exits successfully on Linux PowerShell.
- Publication validates the six release jobs that actually run, preflight plus every Linux, macOS, and Windows architecture, instead of requiring retired per-push CI contexts.

### Security

- Both Windows binaries receive architecture-specific SPDX 2.3 SBOMs, PE-machine validation, and SHA-256 verification before an immutable release is finalized.

## [1.9.0] - 2026-08-04

Provider-neutral usage lanes in `codex-presence-core` 2.0.0 and configuration schema 13, with adaptive quotas, Credits and deterministic Discord composition. Recorded validation covered Windows release contracts, locked workspace gates, RustSec, schema migration, privacy, provider lanes and real Discord SET/CLEAR acknowledgements. The release notes also required Linux, macOS and Windows compile/test gates.

### Added

- `codex-presence-core` 2.0.0 as the UI-free owner of adaptive provider-neutral usage lanes, stream isolation, semantic quota scopes/windows, credits, service tier, session selection, and deterministic two-line Discord composition.
- Canonical parsing for authenticated `account/rateLimits/read` responses, preserving `rateLimitResetCredits` count/details separately from quota windows and keeping protocol `null` versus empty detail states intact.
- Explicit provider usage signals and `UsageSnapshotCollection` preserve Codex, OpenAI API, Claude, and Anthropic streams without cross-lane or cross-account merging; the upstream runtime remains Codex-local.
- Schema 13 field layout for project, branch, model, activity, tokens, cost, quotas, credits, context, and systems, including visibility, zone, order, and compact/descriptive presentation.
- Credits support with explicit zero, unlimited, absent, and malformed input behavior; Credits is enabled in Standard and Full presets and remains individually private.
- Operational TUI usage and privacy surfaces for semantic quota windows, scoped limits, Credits, and `⚡ Fast` presentation.

### Changed

- Usage windows are dynamic and named from each `window_minutes`; arbitrary and weekly-only windows render truthfully without positional `primary`/`secondary` assumptions or fabricated `5h` windows.
- Global-account Credits take precedence within a stream; ambiguous/equal-rank envelopes and unknown lanes fail closed.
- Service-tier authority is active-session evidence first, `config.toml` fallback second, legacy global state third, then explicit unknown/standard behavior.
- Rich Presence composition preserves all observed global/model quota envelopes, omits unavailable values, and enforces Discord's 128-character line boundary deterministically.
- Repository governance now uses YAML issue forms, Conventional Commits, runtime-proof PRs, synchronized SemVer/core/schema release gates, Dependabot, and a Windows SPDX SBOM contract.

### Fixed

- Parser tests no longer depend on a developer's real `models_cache.json`.
- Explicit Standard sessions no longer inherit stale global Fast state.
- Active OpenCode sessions no longer inherit Codex subscription quota or plan evidence from an unrelated session lane.
- Usage-window deserialization rejects missing percentages and non-positive durations instead of fabricating `100% remaining`; provider-reported remaining percentages and individual-account scope are preserved.
- `discord-proof` correlates both SET and CLEAR acknowledgements by nonce, redacts local session identity and hidden costs, and prevents shell setup statements or command arguments from entering the public activity.

### Security

- Release artifacts retain immutable tag/SHA approval and checksum verification; the Windows binary additionally receives a validated SPDX 2.3 SBOM.

- Service-tier authority is active-session evidence first, `config.toml` fallback second, legacy global state third, then explicit unknown/standard behavior.
